error.no_energy_price: An energy price is needed: either type a fixed one or pick an entity that publishes it.

user.title: Your electricity tariff
user.description: Copy the prices from your contract, not from the printed bill: bills round them to three decimals and computing with those is about half a per cent out. Leave anything you are unsure about as it is.

sources.name: Where the kWh come from
sources.description: The meters measuring energy in and out of the house.

data_description.consumption_entity: The meter that accumulates kWh bought from the grid. It needs history: its hourly statistics are what the bill is built from.
data_description.export_entity: Only if you have solar panels. Leave empty if you never export.
data_description.cycle_day: Check the start date on your last bill. The 1st is the usual one.

power.name: Contracted power
power.description: Paid for every day of the month whether you use it or not. The 2.0TD tariff has two periods and you may have contracted a different power in each.

data_description.power_p1_kw: The figure your contract gives for P1. A home is typically between 3.3 and 5.75 kW.
data_description.power_p1_price: Shown on the bill as the peak power term, in euros per kW per day.
data_description.power_p2_kw: The one for P2. Usually the same as peak.
data_description.power_p2_price: Much cheaper than peak: often around a quarter of it.

energy.name: Energy price
energy.description: A fixed price, or an entity publishing it if your tariff is index-linked. Fill both and the entity wins.

data.energy_price_taxed: That entity gives the price with taxes included

data_description.energy_price: What you pay for each kWh bought, before tax.
data_description.energy_price_entity: For tariffs changing every hour, such as PVPC. Its hourly statistics are read, not its value right now.
data_description.energy_price_taxed: Tick this if the entity already includes the electricity tax and VAT; they are stripped back before computing, or every kWh would be taxed twice. The Octopus one, for instance, includes them.

surplus.name: Surplus price
surplus.description: What you are credited for the energy you export. Without panels, leave all of this alone.

data.surplus_price_taxed: That entity gives the price with taxes included

data_description.surplus_price: What you are credited per kWh exported. Leave at 0 if you never export.
data_description.surplus_price_entity: Only if your compensation varies by the hour as well.
data_description.surplus_price_taxed: Careful: it need not match the purchase price. With Octopus the buying price comes with taxes and the surplus price without.

fixed.name: Fixed costs
fixed.description: Items that do not depend on what you use. If you do not know them, look at your last bill and leave them at 0 meanwhile.

data_description.bono_social: Set by the government and the same for everyone, around €0.025 a day.
data_description.meter_rental: Rental of the meter itself, about €0.027 a day.
data_description.monthly_fee: Any add-on service billed monthly: maintenance, home packs and the like.
data_description.monthly_fee_name: How it should read in the breakdown, for example «Home Pack».

taxes.name: Taxes
taxes.description: The values here are the ones in force in Spain. You only need to touch them if they change.

data.tax_includes_bono: Bono social counts towards the electricity tax

data_description.tax_includes_bono: Retailers differ here: Iberdrola includes it, Octopus does not. Check the base your bill applies the electricity tax to.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: For tariffs priced differently by time of day, and for fine-tuning how surplus is treated.

data.surplus_capped: Surplus cannot exceed the energy term
data.hourly_netting: Net imports against exports within each hour

data_description.energy_price_p2: Leave empty if you pay the same around the clock, which is the common case.
data_description.energy_price_p3: Likewise: only if your tariff distinguishes periods.
data_description.surplus_capped: This is what the rules say: compensation can take the energy term to zero, never into your favour.
data_description.hourly_netting: The hourly net balance Spanish law requires: export 3 kWh and import 1 in the same hour and you exported 2.

reconfigure.title: Your electricity tariff
reconfigure.description: You can change anything here, the sensors included. The current cycle is recomputed on save.
